lead: Privacy and usage limits depend on where a system boundary sits: operating-system capture, inference resellers and shared account allowances each expose different constraints. The evening coverage adds renderer-security research and a coding-search project whose own evaluation does not show an average improvement over its first attempt.
Reports of acquisitions, financing and proposed proofs remain separate from completed deals, audited terms or accepted mathematical results.

sections.title: Privacy boundaries depend on the platform
sections.intro: Signal’s own announcement explains why screenshot controls do not cover every route to decrypted application data.

sections.title: Cost proxies and proposed migrations need precise labels
sections.intro: Independent model comparisons and reported geopolitical plans describe different kinds of evidence.

sections.title: A funding claim is not a financing audit
sections.intro: An unrelated profile post, early fundraising talks and an inaccessible market report each limit what can be checked.

sections.title: Personal accounts and episode lists have narrower scope
sections.intro: A discussion of unemployment is not a labor survey, and a podcast topic list is not its argument.

sections.title: The machine running the interface is not the model
sections.intro: A retro computing project makes the boundary between a local harness and remote inference unusually visible.

sections.title: A claim still needs its missing checks
sections.intro: A rushed mathematical write-up and a flattened benchmark table each leave a different verification gap.

sections.title: Organizational plans are not demonstrated outcomes
sections.intro: A new gameplay subsidiary, an inaccessible governance article and an export-rule excerpt establish different amounts of evidence.

sections.title: Prompt exposure needs a traceable path
sections.intro: A canary investigation separates evidence of access from attribution to a particular provider or intermediary.

sections.title: Making state and rights explicit
sections.intro: Replication positions and structured licensing metadata help communicate boundaries without making them universal guarantees.

sections.title: A headline or ratio cannot complete the argument
sections.intro: An inaccessible market report, an interview description and a projected spending comparison each leave important checks open.

sections.title: Daily allowances are not unlimited access
sections.intro: Apple documents shared extra usage and regional exclusions for a future software rollout.

sections.title: A route into a renderer is not the same as a proven exploit
sections.intro: The Upload2Shell index separates tested application chains, configuration prerequisites and paths traced only to the underlying renderer.

sections.title: More attempts and more tokens still need better evaluation
sections.intro: A coding-search project reports disappointing hidden-test results, while a plugin fix makes an expensive reasoning setting available.

sections.title: A notification adds context, not a second experiment
sections.intro: Ars covers the existing canary investigation and reports a routing-provider response, with attribution limits intact.

sections.title: Personal projects and acquisition talks retain their limits
sections.intro: A creator account is not a productivity study, and an indexed deal report is not a completed purchase.
